title: Identify an Unknown Food Sample
question: Which types of biological molecules can you detect in an unknown sample?

blocks.prompt: Required before setup: Could a positive starch test tell you whether U also contains protein? Predict which evidence you would need and explain why.
blocks.text: A positive starch test alone cannot tell whether U has protein. I predict that separate indicators are needed.

blocks.prompt: Required before setup: Why use both positive and negative controls? Explain why each indicator needs a separate portion of the same unknown.
blocks.text: The positive control shows a known response; the negative control shows the blank. Keep the portions separate so indicators do not mix.
Prediction timing: Before setup and observations.

Use one unknown sample divided into separate portions for four different tests. Each test provides different evidence. Model-prepared controls show known comparison results. After placing one portion, you may prepare matched fresh portions without repeating that motion. You must still run and interpret each different test.

Sources: unknown appearances are model-generated; observations and molecule claims are student interpretations. Positive and negative control results are supplied comparison data. They are not independent student trials.

Identify reducing sugars, starch, protein, and lipids from test evidence.

blocks.prompt: Use all four recorded observations to explain which molecule types were detected in U. Compare the results with your prediction.

Support a conclusion while respecting the limits of indicator tests.

blocks.prompt: Does a negative reducing-sugar result prove there are no carbohydrates? Can these tests identify an exact food or exact amounts? Explain the limits using your evidence.
blocks.text: My inference explanation compares the actual observations with both supplied controls. Different indicators detect different targets; not detected is limited by the method.

blocks.prompt: Benedict’s reagent is still blue before heating. What should you conclude?
blocks.text: The test is not ready to interpret; use the required heating step.
Correct! Correct interpretation needs the completed test. Reducing-sugar results are judged after heating and against the known controls. Revised after feedback.

blocks.prompt: What does a negative indicator result establish?
blocks.text: The target was not detected under these test conditions.
Correct! A negative result is limited by the method and its sensitivity. It does not prove that the sample is empty or that all other molecule types are absent. Correct on the first recorded check.

This is a virtual model with synthetic sample compositions and clear test results. Real foods, mixtures, colors, test sensitivity, and contamination can affect a result. Amounts too low to make a clear change may be missed. A negative result means not detected by this test, not proof that the substance is completely absent. These tests do not identify every biological molecule or give exact amounts. Heating, staining, rinsing, and drying are shortened. Drawings and liquid levels are schematic, not measurements. This is not a physical laboratory protocol.
